title: Calorimetry Comet: Measuring ΔH
welcome_lead: Quantify enthalpy changes from temperature shifts.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on calorimetry and bond enthalpy calculations.
final_note: You measured heat one ΔT at a time.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Measure ΔT for known volume of solution. Use mass of solution and c ≈ 4.18 J/g/K.

q = m c ΔT. ΔH per mol = -q / n. Sign: ΔH negative for exothermic.

Spirit burner heats water in calorimeter. q = m(water) c ΔT. Energy released per g of fuel = q / m(fuel).

ΔHc = -(q × Mr) / m(fuel burnt). Always less negative than literature due to heat loss to surroundings and incomplete combustion.

ΔH ≈ Σ bond enthalpies (bonds broken) - Σ bond enthalpies (bonds made).

Bond enthalpies are mean values across many compounds, so result is approximate. Works only for gaseous species.

options: -q / n
q × n
q + n
q / m

mcqs.q: In an exothermic reaction, what happens energetically with the bonds?
options: All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
Bond breaking releases energy and bond making absorbs energy.
Energy released forming new bonds exceeds energy absorbed breaking existing bonds.

mcqs.q: Why can an endothermic reaction still be spontaneous?
options: Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.
All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.
If the entropy increase (TΔS) is large enough to outweigh the positive ΔH, ΔG can still be negative.
Endothermic reactions are never spontaneous because they require energy input.

mcqs.q: Why is the hydration enthalpy of a small, highly charged ion very exothermic?
options: All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.
Small/highly charged ions form strong ion-dipole attractions with water molecules, releasing a large amount of energy.
Hydration enthalpy only depends on the size of the ion, not its charge.
Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.
